fact: Minister of ICT Savannah Maziya said Eswatini is set to launch a nationwide coding program to train more than 300,000 citizens in digital skills.

The Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade launched the Macetjeni iHub on 6 August 2026, set up by SEDCO with ESCCOM and UNDP, to give beneficiaries training in computer literacy, Microsoft Office, AI and digital marketing.

Principal Secretary at the Ministry of ICT Prince Mshishimba said government is to introduce AI, robotics, coding and cybersecurity training at community innovation hubs, moving beyond basic digital literacy training, with a new iHub being prepared in Shiselweni.

The Government of Eswatini and UNDP launched the Macetjeni iHub on 6 August 2026, a centre offering digital skills training to young people, women, small business owners and persons with disabilities.
The hub enrolled a first cohort of 15 in a basic computer skills programme in June 2026 and completed the two-month course by end of July, per its manager.
The ICT minister said Coders Eswatini, implemented through cooperation with the UAE, aims to equip 300,000 emaSwati with internationally recognised digital skills, at least half women.

Prime Minister Dlamini said Eswatini is investing in digital skills development, including coding, data science and AI education for young people, under its National Fourth Industrial Revolution Strategy.
